אמר ההדיוט הכותב בדברי הרב בהג״ה ראיתי לבאר קצת מ״ש ולא בעגול בד״מ כתב כמו שעושין בב״ה שנועצים מסמורים א״י אם ר״ל נועצים מסמורים בכותל בעיגול או סביב לוח א׳ עגול נועצים מסמורים בעיגול ואיך שיהיה איזה הפרש יש בין פמוט לזה וי״ל וע׳ פר״ח. והנה תראה שהר״ב ז״ל בד״מ כתב שכל א׳ מובדל מחבירו לא מיקרי מדורה וכאן כ׳ מובדל הרבה מחבירו ובתה״ד ק״ה כ״ב דלא דמי פמוט לקערה שכל קנה מובדל במחיצה ועוד לבעל העיטור בקערה רחוק ב׳ אצבעות שרי וכאן רחוק הרבה יע״ש. והמחבר אוסר בקערה אפילו רחוק הרבה כהטור והר״ב מדשתיק אודויי אודי ליה אלא בפמוט החמיר דבעינן שיהיו מובדלין הקנים וגם הרבה רחוקים יותר מב׳ אצבעות הא בחסר א׳ דהיינו שאין מובדלין במחיצות או מובדלין ואין רחוקים הקנים זה מזה ב׳ אצבעות אסור דהוי כמדורה. וא״כ צ״ע כשמדבקין נרות שעוה בכותל באין רחוקים ב׳ אצבעות די״ל דאסור ועא״ר בטור אצבע ובתה״ד ב׳ אצבעות ואי״ה במ״א ג״ד יבואר עוד:

turei_zahav.he: ואפי' אם רבים. דבגמ' איתא מהדרין מן המהדרין בה"א מוסיף והולך ופי' התו' דזה קאי אנר איש וביתו דהיינו שכל הבית אין להם אלא נר א' בליל הראשון ממילא כשרואין בבית שני נרות בליל ב' ירגישו בתוס' הנס אבל לאותן שמדליקים בלילה הראשונה נר לכל א' מבני הבית אז אם ידליקו בליל שני ב' לכל א' אין כאן הכרה לתוס' הנס כי יאמרו שיש הרבה בני בית ולכל א' אין שם רק נר אחת וזהו דעת הטור והש"ע אבל הרמב"ם פי' שאף לאותן שמדליקין נר לכל אחד יעשו לכל א' ב' נרות בליל שני וכן עד ח' וזהו הי"א של רמ"א ובכאן יש חידוש במנהג שהספרדים נוהגין כתוס' כמ"ש [ב"י] והאשכנזים כרמב"ם וזה לא מצינו בשאר מקומות:

yad_ephraim.he: סק"ו נתקשו רבים כו' וצד ששם הציר הוא צד השני כו' ר"ל וכשאדם עומד בפנים אז הימין שלו מכוון נגד הציר ושמאלו נגד המזוזה וכשעומד בחוץ אז הוא להיפוך שימינו נגד המזוזה ושמאלו נגד הציר וכשעומד לפנים אז שייך לקרות לחלק הציר כניסה לפי שהוא קרוב לפנים לבית והחלק הקרוב למזוזה הוא חיצון ולפי פירוש הראשון שהאדם בפנים וא"כ החלק הקרוב לפנים קרוי כניסה דהיינו לצד הציר והוא נגד ימין האדם א"כ אפשר לפרש לצד שמאל נגד האדם כמו לפירושיהם דזה אינו דא"כ יהי' הדלק' קרוב למזוזה שהרי לפי פירוש זה שהאדם בפנים שמאל האדם למזוזה וזה לא מסתבר וע"כ לפרש דהך שמאל אינו רק מה שהוא שמאל בעלמא דהיינו לצד הציר כדאמרינן נר חנוכה בשמאל ומזוזה בימין וא"כ כשאמר מחציה של כניסה שהכוונה באותו חצי של צד הציר שוב מה בא להוסיף בתנאי השני שיהי' לצד שמאל אלא ע"כ שר"ל שבאותו חלק עצמו יהי' לצד שמאל דהיינו בקצה האחרון סמך לכותל וזה כוונת הט"ז מ"ש בסוף משא"כ לפירוש שאדרבא כו' ובמשבצות זהב כת' לפירוש הראשון שבחלק הכניסה יניח לצד שמאל דהיינו אותו צד שסמוך לחלק הקרוב למזוזה שהוא צד שמאל של האדם כשעומד בפנים ע"ש וזה אינו שהרי הט"ז מסיים להדיא שיהי' בקצה האחרון סמוך לכותל כו' ודבר ברור כמ"ש דלפירוש הראשון אין פירוש לצד שמאל מה שהיא נקרא שמאל נגד האדם שא"כ יתקרב יותר לצד המזוזה וזה אינו אלא פירושו לצד שמאל מה שנקרא שמאל הפתח בכל מקום דהיינו לצד ציר הפתח:
yad_ephraim.en: (106) Many were perplexed, etc., and the side where the hinge is is the second side, etc. — meaning: when a person stands inside, his right faces the hinge and his left the mezuzah; when he stands outside it is reversed, his right toward the mezuzah and his left toward the hinge. When standing inside, the part of the hinge may be called the entrance side because it is closer to the inside of the house, and the part near the mezuzah is the outer side. Per the first explanation that the person is inside — if so the part close to the inside is called entrance, i.e. toward the hinge side, which is opposite the man's right; one could then explain "to the left relative to the man" as in their explanation — but this is not so, for then the lighting would be close to the mezuzah, since per this explanation when the man is inside his left is toward the mezuzah, and this is not reasonable. Therefore explain that this "left" is only left in the ordinary sense, i.e. toward the hinge side, as we say: Chanukah candle on the left and mezuzah on the right. If so, when he said half of the entrance he means that half on the hinge side — why then add the second condition that it be to the left? Rather it must mean that within that same part it should be to the left, i.e. at the far end near the wall — and this is the Taz's intent in what he wrote at the end. Not like the explanation that on the contrary, etc. And in Mishbetzos Zahav he wrote per the first explanation that in the entrance part one places it to the left, i.e. that side adjacent to the part near the mezuzah, which is the man's left side when standing inside — but this is not so, for the Taz concludes explicitly that it should be at the far end near the wall, etc. And it is clear as he wrote that per the first explanation there is no explanation of "left" as left relative to the man, for then it would be closer to the mezuzah side, which is not so; rather his explanation is "left" as the opening is called left everywhere, i.e. toward the hinge side of the door:

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ג] מוסיף והולך וכו'. נראה לי דמי שאין לו שמן הרבה יתן באחד שמן כשיעור וממותר יחלק לכולם שאם יעשה לכולם בשוה לא ידליק אפילו אחד כשיעור, ואם יש לו שמן בצמצום ולחבירו אין לו כלל מוטב שידליק בכל לילה אחד ויתן גם לחבירו דהא מדינא אין צריך אלא אחד (מגן אברהם). ולכאורה קשה הא גם לחבירו מדינא אין צריך דכל בני ביתו מדליקין מדינא אחד ואפשר דמיירי שאינו מבני ביתו, ועוד יש לומר דעל כל פנים צריך להשתתף והוא רוצה שידליק לבדו עיין ס"ק ט' וסימן תרע"ז סעיף ג'. אך צריך עיון בתשובת בית יעקב סימן קי"ז שפסק דאין לאדם להשאיל טלית לחבירו בכפר או לזכות באתרוג שלו אף שיכול לצאת בשל חבירו דניחא ליה וכו' טפי לברך על שלו, עד כאן, והכא נמי רוצה שיהא מן המהדרין ודוחק לחלק. מיהו בסימן תרנ"ח ס"ק י"ב העליתי דלא כתשובת בית יעקב. והנה בתשובת שער אפרים סימן מ"ב למה אין נוהגין שאשה מדלקת כשבעל בביתו מאי שנא משאר בני הבית עיין שם. ונראה לי דאשתו כגופו ואינו בכלל מהדרין וכן משמע ברש"ל סימן פ"ה ומטה משה, דדוקא כשאין לה בעל או כשאין הבעל בעיר מדלקת ועיין סימן תרע"ז ס"ק ד' וכן משמע בראב"ן סימן (שמ"ז)[ש"מ]:
eliyah_rabbah.en: [C] Adds and goes, etc. It seems to me that a person who does not have a lot of oil should give oil to one person as a share and it is permissible to distribute it to everyone. If he does it to everyone in equal measure, he will not light even one as a share. And apparently it's difficult, isn't it also necessary for his fellow countrymen to have the members of his family light one country, and it is possible for a demiri who is not one of his family members, and it should also be said that in any case, he should participate and he wants to be lit alone, see section 9 and the sign of 1977, section 3. But it is necessary to study the response of Beit Ya'akov sign 17, which ruled that a person may lend a tallit to his friend in the village or to be entitled to his Ethrog, even though he can go out because of his friend, Danikha Lia, etc. Tafi to bless his own, so far, and here Nami wants it to be from the strict and urges to share. And here is the answer to Sha'ar Ephraim Siman 22 Why is it not customary for a woman to light a candle when her husband is in his house because he hates the rest of the household, see there. And it seems to me that his dash is like his body and is not at all strict, and it also means in Rashel Siman 55 and Mata Moshe, even when she does not have a husband or when the husband is not in the city, she lights a light and see Siman 17, Sec 4, and also the meaning of Rabbin Siman (Shem7):

kaf_hachayim.en: (6) [Seif 2] How many candles one kindles, etc. In the Gemara (Shabbat 21b) it states: The Sages taught — the mitzvah of Chanukah is one candle for a man and his household; those who are mehaderin kindle a candle for each and every one; those who are mehaderin from among the mehaderin — Beit Hillel say: on the first day one kindles one, from there onward one adds and continues. Tosafot explain that this refers to "a candle for a man and his household" — meaning all members of the household have only one candle on the first night; consequently when they see two candles in the house on the second night they will sense the addition of the miracle. But for those who kindle on the first night a candle for each member of the household — if on the second night they kindle two for each one, there is no recognition here of the addition of the miracle, for they will say there are many household members and each has only one candle there. This is the view of Tur and Shulchan Aruch. But Rambam explained that even for those who kindle a candle for each one, they make for each one two candles on the second night, and so on until eight — and this is the second view that Rama wrote in the gloss. And here there is a novelty in custom: Sephardim practice like Tosafot and Ashkenazim like Rambam, which we do not find in other places. Taz s.k. 1. And this is not a novelty, for Rambam himself (chapter 4 of Chanukah) wrote that they practice thus — and not as some wrote regarding the law per se, see there; if so, this is an early custom. [מהרי"ל]:
mechaber.en: It is a mitzvah to place [the Hanukkah light] in the handsbreadth closest to the entrance on the left, so as to have the mezuzah on the right and the Hanukkah light on the left. But if there is no mezuzah in the entrance, he should place [the Hanukkah light] on the right. If one places it in the doorway itself, he should place it on the leftmost half of the entrance. Rem"a: However nowadays, when all kindle inside, and there is no distinction for the people of the public domain at all, one should not worry so much if we do not kindle it in the handsbreadth closest to the entrance. In any case, the custom is to kindle it in the handsbreadth closest to the entrance, as in [our ancestors'] days, and one should not deviate; unless the household members are many, [in which case] it is preferable for each one to kindle in a unique place rather than mixing the lights together, with no distinction of the number of lights they are kindling. In any case, they should take care not to kindle in the same place where they kindle lights all year, since then there would be no distinction at all. And even though there is only no distinction except for the members of the household, some distinction at least is necessary. In the synagogue, one should place [the Hanukkah light] at the southern wall (or to the south of the lamp, and he should arrange them from east to west). (Terumat Hadeshen Section 104, Beit Yosef) We kindle and recite the benedictions (in the synagogue) for the sake of publicizing the miracle. Rem"a: A person does not fulfill his obligation with the lights of the synagogue, and needs to kindle again in his own house. (Isaac ben Sheshet Section 111) We have the custom to kindle in the synagogue between the afternoon prayer and the evening prayer. Some have the custom to kindle on the Sabbath Eve before the afternoon prayer. (Kol Bo and Book of Abudirham) If [the prayer leader] wants to quickly pray right away after [he] has recited the benedictions and kindled one of them, the synagogue attendant may kindle the rest, and the prayer leader may pray. (Jacob ben Moses Moelin)

(לז) ומ"מ המנהג וכו' - כדי שיכנס בין שתי מצות:
(לח) ואין לשנות - ומ"מ אם יש לו חלון הסמוך לר"ה נכון יותר שיניחנו שם כדי שיהיה היכר לבני ר"ה ויתפרסם הנס אם לא במקום דשכיחא הזיקא עי"ז:

mishnah_berurah.en:
(31) Within the tefach adjacent, etc. - For if he distances it further from the entrance, it is not recognizable that the homeowner placed it there.
(32) To the entrance - Whether the placement is at the entrance of the house or at the entrance of the courtyard.
(33) So that it will be, etc. - So that he will be surrounded by mitzvot. Nevertheless, after the fact, if he placed the Chanukkah lamp on the right, he has fulfilled.
(34) And if there is none, etc., on the right - For in every mitzvah matter the right is preferable; furthermore, there is greater publicizing of the miracle, since everyone turns to the right.
(35) And if he placed it in the door itself, etc. - This refers to the beginning of the seif.
(36) From half of the entrance, etc. - Meaning the place of the door through which one enters the house should be divided in two, and in the half that leans to the left side, opposite the mezuzah, which is on the right, there he should place it, as the Magen Avraham writes. This implies that he may place it anywhere in that half. See the Taz, whose view is that in practice it is proper to be stringent and place the lamps on the left side at the far end near the wall.
(37) Nevertheless, the custom, etc. - So that he enters between two mitzvot.
(38) And one should not change - Nevertheless, if he has a window adjacent to the public domain, it is better to place it there so that it will be visible to people in the public domain and the miracle will be publicized, unless this is a place where danger is common because of it.
(39) And in the synagogue - Or in the study hall.
(40) On the southern wall - Or on the table standing near the southern wall. The reason for all this is as a remembrance of the Menorah, whose place in the Mikdash was in the south.
(41) Like the lamps of the Menorah - Or south of the Menorah. This is a scribal error, and it should read: like the lamps of the Menorah.
(42) And he arranges them from east, etc. - This too is like the Menorah, for the lamps in the Mikdash were arranged from east to west, and so he should arrange the Chanukkah lamps. Know that some Rishonim hold that although the Menorah stood in the south, its lamps were arranged from north to south; according to them, the Chanukkah lamps should also be arranged in this way. Some places have practiced so, and one should not protest, for they have what to rely on.
(43) To the west - The one lighting stands with his back to the south and his face to the north, and begins from his right, which is the lamp near the aron kodesh; then he adds progressively, beginning from the leftmost and turning to his right, as Responsa Chatam Sofer siman 186 writes. See below at the end of siman 676, where we will write about this.
(44) And they light and bless - Although in the synagogue it is only a custom, nevertheless they bless over it, just as they bless over Hallel of Rosh Chodesh, which is only a custom. If a mourner leads prayers on the evening of Chanukkah, another person should light the lamps because Shehecheyanu is recited then, and it is recognizable as an expression of joy for the congregation, so it is not fitting that the mourner light them. But at home he may recite Shehecheyanu. On the other evenings of Chanukkah, when Shehecheyanu is not recited, the mourner may light the Chanukkah lamp. A mourner leads Minchah and Maariv on Chanukkah. On the fifteenth of Av and Shevat, and on Lag BaOmer, when there is no Hallel, the mourner also leads Shacharit. On Chol HaMoed, which is like Yom Tov, I have sometimes prevented the mourner from leading Minchah and Maariv, as Peri Megadim writes.
(45) And he must go back and light - Even the shaliach tzibbur who blessed in the synagogue must go back and light in his home, for each person has an obligation to light in his home. Nevertheless, he should not repeat Shehecheyanu at home unless he is lighting to discharge the obligation of his wife and household.
(46) To light in the synagogue between Minchah and Maariv - Meaning that even those who practice to light every day in the synagogue at tzeit hakochavim light after Minchah, when the people are gathered. Also, after Maariv it is not proper to delay the people for this, since each person must hurry home to light the Chanukkah lamp.
(47) Before Minchah - So wrote Maharshal. But in Darkei Moshe he wrote that we do not practice so; rather, even on erev Shabbat we light in the synagogue between Minchah and Maariv, when the people begin to gather and there is publicizing of the miracle. However, if the people are delayed in coming, and before a minyan comes to the synagogue the day will become sanctified, he should not wait at all, but should bless and light immediately, even before Minchah, for in any event there is publicizing of the miracle when they later come to the synagogue and see the lamps. Regarding an individual, see below at the end of siman 679 in Mishna Berurah.
(48) If he wants to hurry, etc. - This is specifically in this manner; otherwise, it is better that he himself complete the mitzvah he began.
(49) The shamash may, etc. - For the blessing takes effect on the one lamp that he lit, which is the essential matter, and the rest are only an enhancement of the mitzvah. The same applies at home: if some urgent matter arises after he has lit one of them, another may complete the remaining lamps for him.
